speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; to begin our assessment, can you describe any specific symptoms you've noticed since birth, such as jaundice, feeding difficulties, or abnormal movements?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis seems incorrect; bluish macules that do not blanch, combined with a continuous heart murmur, cloudy lenses, and hearing loss, strongly suggest a vascular anomaly. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin lesion close-up.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram Findings: Patent ductus arteriosus; Skin lesion close-up: Several bluish macules that do not blanch upon application of pressure

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The classic triad of cataracts (cloudy lenses), sensorineural deafness, and a patent ductus arteriosus (continuous murmur), combined with non-blanching "blueberry muffin" rash, is pathognomonic for this condition. Blood culture results are expected to be negative, as this is a congenital infection, not cellulitis.
